raw_case_text:
Five-year-old female patient with a history of Down syndrome, from the province of Quillabamba, department of Cusco, an Amazon jungle area endemic for leishmaniasis. Her father reported that, at the age of one year, the child began to develop papular lesions on the face, which slowly increased in size. One year after their appearance, the lesions ulcerated near the malar and mandibular region on the right side of the face. The patient was transferred and diagnosed with cutaneous leishmaniasis at the Regional Hospital of Cusco in June 2016, where she was treated with amphotericin B deoxycholate at a dosage of 7 mg every 24 h for 37 days (cumulative dose of 259 mg); she showed little improvement after treatment.
In 2017, the patient was admitted to a different level III hospital in Cusco due to multiple lesions on the face, buttock, lower limbs, elbow, right hand, respiratory distress and laryngeal stridor. Amphotericin B deoxycholate was administered at a dose of 9 mg every 24 hr for five months (cumulative dose of 952.4 mg). She also received sodium stibogluconate for 25 days, imiquimod daily and miltefosine at 30 mg/day for two months (weight: 12 kg). Response to treatment was poor, with persistent ulcers on the right elbow and face, laryngeal stridor and dysphonia; despite treatment, new lesions appeared on the left thigh. Subsequently, the patient was lost to follow-up, although in 2018, she received 10 mg/day of prednisone for three months at a healthcare facility.
On January 2019, the patient was admitted again to the Regional Hospital of Cusco and then referred to the National Institute of Child Health in Lima because of the increasing size of the lesions (Figures 1A and 2A). Multiple ulcers with infiltrated raised borders were found during physical examination, these lesions were distributed on the buttocks, elbows, arms, legs and chin, with diameters ranging from 1 cm in the arms and legs to 8 cm in the buttocks. Erosions in the oral mucosa of 0.5 cm, subcostal retractions and diffuse rhonchi in both lungs were also found. No other signs and symptoms were found during examination.
Skin biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis, irregular epidermal hyperplasia, fibrous dermis with predominantly dense, lymphohistiocytic, inflammatory infiltrate with some plasma cells, and histiocytes with abundant structures suggestive of Leishmania spp. amastigotes. Amastigote forms were found during direct microscopic examination (smear test); this procedure was carried out at the National Referral Laboratory of Leishmaniasis of the National Institute of Health since the periodic acid-Schiff stain (PAS) and the differentiation group 1A (CD1A) were negative. The Montenegro intradermal reaction test (IDRM) was positive, with a 7 x 8 mm induration at 48 hrs. Anti-Leishmania IgG antibodies were detected in the patients' serum by indirect immunofluorescence, with a positive titer of 1/160.
Genomic DNA samples extracted from lesion tissue revealed that the disease was caused by Leishmania (Viannia) braziliensis. Using a polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphisms (PCR-RFLP) technique, the region of the gene encoding the heat shock protein (Hsp70) was amplified and then subjected to an enzymatic digestion process with HaeIII and RsaI, according to the methodology described by Montalvo et al. in 2012 (Figures 3 and 4). Flow cytometry analysis was carried out at the National Referral Center for Allergy, Asthma and Immunology (CERNAAI) and at the Immunology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of the Peruvian Cayetano Heredia University. Laboratory tests showed the following: total leukocytes: 4600 cells/microL, CD3/CD4 lymphocytes: 258 cells/microL (normal range: 500-2700), regulatory T lymphocytes: 14 cells/microL (normal range: 35-140), T Helper CD4 lymphocytes: 251 cells/microL (normal range: 1500-5000 cells/microL), CD8 Cytotoxic T cells: 627 cells/microL (normal range: 500-1600 cells/microL), B lymphocytes: 50 cells/microL (normal range: 600-3000 cells/microL), and Natural Killer (NK) lymphocytes: 195 cells/microL (normal range: 100-1300 cells/microL).
The patient was diagnosed with DL and treatment started with liposomal amphotericin B, 3 mg/kg/day intravenously every 5 to 6 days, she received 15 doses. Dermal infections were also treated. Patients' condition improved after the 11th dose (Figures 1B and 2B), up until the 15th dose (Figure 2C).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 5-year-old girl with Down syndrome from Quillabamba, Cusco, Peru, presented in January 2019 with progressively enlarging, treatment-refractory multiple ulcerated cutaneous lesions across the face, buttocks, extremities, and oral mucosa accompanied by respiratory distress.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed facial papules at 1 year of age that ulcerated over the right malar and mandibular region by age 2. Diagnosed with cutaneous leishmaniasis in June 2016, she had poor responses to multiple treatment courses between 2016 and 2018—including amphotericin B deoxycholate (259 mg cumulative in 2016; 952.4 mg cumulative over 5 months in 2017), sodium stibogluconate (25 days), topical imiquimod, oral miltefosine (30 mg/day for 2 months), and prednisone (10 mg/day for 3 months in 2018)—with new and enlarging ulcers on the buttocks, limbs, elbow, right hand, and chin, plus laryngeal stridor and dysphonia, prompting referral to the National Institute of Child Health in Lima in January 2019.
subjective.past_medical_history: Down syndrome; from Quillabamba province, Cusco department, an Amazonian jungle region endemic for leishmaniasis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for multiple skin ulcers, oral mucosal lesions, dysphonia, laryngeal stridor, and respiratory distress.

objective.physical_examination: Multiple ulcers with infiltrated raised borders distributed over the buttocks, elbows, arms, legs, and chin (ranging from 1 cm on the limbs to 8 cm on the buttocks), 0.5 cm oral mucosal erosions, subcostal retractions, and diffuse bilateral pulmonary rhonchi.
objective.advanced_workup: Flow cytometry immunophenotyping showed CD4+ T-lymphopenia (CD3/CD4 258 cells/uL, ref 500-2700; T-helper CD4 251 cells/uL, ref 1500-5000), reduced regulatory T cells (14 cells/uL, ref 35-140), and severe B-cell lymphopenia (50 cells/uL, ref 600-3000), with normal CD8+ T cells (627 cells/uL, ref 500-1600) and NK cells (195 cells/uL, ref 100-1300). Skin biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis, irregular epidermal hyperplasia, and a dense dermal lymphohistiocytic and plasmacytic infiltrate containing abundant amastigote-like structures (PAS and CD1a negative).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Direct smear microscopy identified Leishmania spp. amastigotes, Montenegro intradermal test was positive (7 x 8 mm induration at 48 h), serum anti-Leishmania IgG IIF was positive (titer 1:160), and Hsp70 PCR-RFLP (HaeIII and RsaI digestion) confirmed disseminated cutaneous leishmaniasis (DL) caused by Leishmania (Viannia) braziliensis in the setting of Down syndrome-associated cellular and humoral immunodeficiency. Treatment with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day every 5-6 days for 15 doses) plus management of secondary dermal infections produced marked clinical regression of the ulcers from the 11th through 15th doses.
